chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you have finished with the supplication by the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then go to the Pulpit, wipe it with your hand, and hold its two pomegranates (which are the Soflawan), and wipe your eyes and your face with them, for it is said that it is a healing for the eyes.

And stand by it, so praise Allah and extol Him, and ask your need, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'What is between my Pulpit and my house is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my Pulpit is upon a channel from the channels of Paradise, and the channel is the small door.'

Then you go to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and pray therein whatever comes to you. So when you enter the Masjid, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And when you exit, do the same, and frequent praying in the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.السُّفْلَاوَان: A type of ceramic or porcelain, referring to the material of the Pulpit's pomegranates
key_terms.الْمِنْبَر: The Pulpit or pulpit of the Prophet
key_terms.تُرْعَةٌ: A channel or waterway, metaphorically used for the blessed area
key_terms.رَوْضَةٌ: A garden or meadow, specifically referring to the area between the Prophet's house and Pulpit

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals and etiquettes when visiting the Prophet's grave and Pulpit in Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the spiritual etiquette of visiting the Prophet’s grave, emphasizing the Minbar as a locus of barakah where wiping it is believed to cure eye ailments, rooted in the Prophet’s description of the space between his house and Minbar as a 'garden of Paradise.' It further instructs believers to pray at the specific Maqam (place) of the Prophet and to abundantly send blessings (Salawat) upon him upon entering and exiting the Masjid, reinforcing the connection between physical proximity to the Prophet and spiritual elevation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Safwan Bin yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you are free from the supplication by the grave of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, then go to the Pulpit and wipe it with your hand, and grab its two pomegranates, and they are both ceramic, and wipe your eyes and your face with it, for it is said that it is a healing for the eyes.

And stand by it, so Praise Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Extoll upon Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and ask your need, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What is between my<sup>as</sup> Pulpit and my<sup>saww</sup> house, there is a garden from the Gardens of the Paradise, and my<sup>saww</sup> Pulpit is a channel from the channels of the Paradise, and the channel, it is the small door.

Then go to the place of the Prophetsaww, and Pray Salaat therein whatever come to you. So when you enter the Masjid, then send Blessings upon the Prophetsaww. And when you exit, so do similar to that, and frequent from the Praying of Salaat in the Masjid of the Rasool-Allahsaww’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘When you complete your prayer near the grave of the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, then go to the pulpit. You should touch it with your hand, hold the two pomegranates, which are made of ceramic materials and wipe your hand over your eyes and face. It is said that it is cure for the eyes.

Then stand up near the pulpit, thank and praise Allah and ask for your wishes. The Messenger of Allah has said, “Between my pulpit and my house there is a garden of the gardens of paradise and my pulpit is a Tur‘ah (passage) of the passage of paradise.” Al-Tur‘a is a small door.

Thereafter you should go to the station of the Holy Prophet, perform salat (prayer) as much as you like. When you enter the Masjid, then say, “O Allah, grant salawat (favors and compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause). When you leave do as you just had done. In the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah, perform as many salat (prayer) as you can.”
